A green battery means the AUTHOR's work is done; only his own eye makes something ACCEPTED. No document in this corpus may claim his approval unless it carries a <!-- CEO-OK: <id> --> marker naming an entry here. ledger-truth.mjs fails the battery on an unregistered claim. The trigger for this register was his own example: the board said the rival analysis was done and approved, and he had never approved it — he inspected it himself and rejected it.
_fields: date = when he said it. what = what he approved, in plain words. verbatim = HIS OWN WORDS, or null when nobody wrote them down. conditions = what he attached to it. where = the record that carries the approval.
_null_verbatim: A null verbatim is not a defect to hide — it is an entry the CEO may legitimately dispute, because no one captured his sentence. It stays registered so the claim is visible and challengeable, never deleted quietly.

construction-company-db-separation-2026-.what: The three decisions that govern the separation of the construction database from the holding's own database. (1) TWO SEPARATE ENGINES: the construction site gets its own Postgres instance in its own container, on its own port, with its own credentials, named DxB_Build; the company keeps the Supabase stack it is already in; there is no path from one to the other. He approved this WAY ROUND on the same day, after the measurement showed the first way round would break his live surfaces (ten components subscribe to Supabase Realtime, his login is Supabase Auth, and the Supabase CLI pins the database name to postgres) — the earlier direction, that the company would move, is withdrawn and no build ever ran under it. (2) THE CLONE IS A MODEL, NOT A MIRROR: the construction database is built from schema plus generated seed and carries none of the company's real rows; where a test must measure the real company it looks through a one-way window, a separate role holding SELECT and nothing else, enforced by database privilege rather than by code. (3) THE ACCUMULATED RESIDUE IS MOVED, NOT DELETED: a dated full dump first, then every construction-origin row moves to a separate dxb_archive database, each move written to audit_log, and the door is walled so the company's records cannot refill with construction traffic.

Three adversarial audits had rejected Block 3, and the third named the reason: every attempt had built the wall inside PostgreSQL while the construction runtime held the Docker socket (root on this machine), every credential file and a direct TCP login. He was told exactly that, in his own language, with the measurements in front of him — docker exec reaching supabase_admin as a true superuser, the owner role able to INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE every company table, three credential files readable, a working TCP login, and the governance gate itself reading the holding through that same socket with a fallback as the owner of everything.
